name: Epitalon

lead: Epitalon (epithalon) is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) developed from an extract of bovine pineal gland by a Russian research group. It is sold as a research chemical.

It is popular in anti-aging communities because of claims that it lengthens telomeres. Most data come from the originating group, animal studies and cell lines, with no large independent human trials.

paras: Cell studies report that epitalon can upregulate telomerase or alternative lengthening of telomeres, and it has been proposed to affect melatonin production and gene expression. Whether these mechanisms translate into human anti-aging effects has not been validated.

Human safety data are small and mostly from one research group. It is not approved as a drug by major regulators, product quality is unregulated, and telomerase activation raises theoretical cancer concerns.
